honest.t: Hepatic arterial infusion converts unresectable disease.
honest.why: What is actually known is high hepatic response in single-arm, centre-concentrated series with no randomised conversion endpoint. The 47% conversion rate comes from a 49-patient phase I experience at one high-volume pump centre, where resectability was adjudicated by the surgeons who then operated, response was scored by WHO-type criteria rather than RECIST, median disease-free survival after R0 resection was 7.6 months, and more than half the resected patients needed portal vein embolisation or intraoperative ablation. The Dutch phase II study met a feasibility endpoint, not an efficacy one, and its 83% disease control rate is not comparable with the 37–58% complete local treatment CAIRO5 achieved on systemic therapy alone. Selection turns on liver-dominant burden, arterial anatomy, prior therapy and pump programme maturity, and the programme commits to tracking the conversion-to-resection rate, biliary toxicity and 6-month grade 3 or worse toxicity.

honest.t: Ablation and resection are equivalent for small lesions.
honest.why: For lesions of 3 cm or less in selected patients, COLLISION's early stopping satisfied its own prespecified rule — a 90.5% conditional likelihood of proving non-inferiority — but formal overall-survival non-inferiority was not shown: the HR was 1.05 with a 95% CI of 0.69–1.58, whose upper bound crosses the trial's own 1.30 margin, and 5-year survival was 51.2% after ablation against 58.0% after resection. It enrolled few high-burden patients (intermediate n=91, high n=21), allowed combined ablation and resection in both arms, excluded solitary deep lesions needing major hepatectomy by mid-trial amendment, and was funded by an ablation device manufacturer. ESMO 2026 nevertheless recommends ablation over resection below 3 cm [II, B] without qualifying for lesion position or achievable margin. Selection turns on lesion size and location, achievable margin, remnant considerations and operator experience, and the programme tracks local progression by achieved margin band and salvage feasibility after ablation failure.

honest.t: ALPPS expands curative options.
honest.why: LIGRO randomised 100 patients and analysed 97, showing a higher resection rate (92% versus 57%); long-term oncologic outcome was not the endpoint and is reported in a separate paper, and the authors state the oncologic role is therefore uncertain. Rescue ALPPS after failed portal vein occlusion closed most of the gap (82% versus 92%, not significant), so the trial does not rule out an embolisation-first strategy. Ninety-day mortality was 8.3% versus 6.1% with liver failure in all seven deaths, severe complications were 43% in both arms, and resectability assessment, volumetry and embolisation technique were all left to local practice. Selection turns on remnant volume, biology, fitness and dropout risk in a staged approach, and the programme tracks resection rate, 90-day mortality, R0 rate and 2-year recurrence.

honest.t: Transplantation should be offered beyond TransMet criteria.
honest.why: There is no randomised evidence outside that population, and the single randomised trial recruited 94 patients in 5.5 years across 20 centres after an independent panel rejected 40% of those local boards thought eligible. Selection turns on the Oslo score, CEA, largest lesion, metabolic tumour volume, interval from the primary and donor strategy — all of them one centre's prognostic work rather than validated gates — and the commitment is a mandatory registry recording whether criteria were met or exceeded, recurrence site and post-recurrence survival.

honest.t: Surgical reassessment every 8 weeks improves outcome.
honest.why: It is an operating judgement with no comparative evidence for the interval. ESMO asks for reassessment every 2–3 months on first-line treatment and the Chinese 2024 consensus every 1.5–2.0 months; neither interval was derived or tested. Selection turns on regimen, tempo of response, patient tolerance and scheduling capacity, and the programme tracks the conversion rate and the time from first response to operation.

honest.t: There is one set of criteria for transplanting colorectal liver metastases.
honest.why: There are at least four, and they disagree on gates that decide individual patients. The OPTN guidance route requires BRAF wild type, microsatellite stability, 12 months from CRLM diagnosis, six months of stability or regression, CEA at or below 80 µg/L and no pretreatment lesion above 10 cm. IHPBA 2021 adds exclusion for metabolic tumour volume above 70 cm³ with total lesion glycolysis above 260 g, bars MSI-high and mismatch-repair-deficient patients outright, limits the BRAF exclusion to V600E, and excludes undifferentiated and signet-ring histology. ESMO 2026 asks only for stabilisation of three months or more no later than third line and sets no MSI and no PET-volume bar at all. TransMet's own entry criteria are a fifth filter again. A dMMR patient with four months of stability and a metabolic tumour volume of 90 cm³ is transplantable under ESMO and barred under IHPBA and the OPTN route; a non-V600E BRAF-mutant patient is eligible under IHPBA and excluded by the OPTN wording. The roadmap's rule that the stricter governs is a defensible institutional choice, but it is a choice, not a finding — no study compares these filters against each other, and none of the thresholds was derived in a cohort large enough to validate it.

honest.t: The Oslo score, the 70 cm³ metabolic tumour volume cut-off and the CEA 80 µg/L bar are validated selection tools.
honest.why: They are one programme's numbers, tested largely in the patients from which they were derived. The Oslo score was derived from the first 21 SECA-I patients who then reappear in every later analysis; the 70 cm³ threshold was set by ROC analysis in the same 40-patient cohort in which it is tested; the CEA 80 µg/L cutoff comes from SECA-I. In the 19-patient score comparison, every patient with a Fong score of 0–2 also had a metabolic tumour volume below 70 cm³ and an Oslo score of 0–2, so the three scores cannot be told apart and no multivariable model exists; in the 61-patient cohort, factors were tested one at a time by log-rank with no correction for multiple testing. The PET signal held only when the scan was within 90 days of transplant and was not significant beyond that. None of this has been reproduced at another centre, and IHPBA 2021 nonetheless carries 70 cm³ and 260 g forward as binary exclusions.

honest.t: Permanent unresectability is a determination this pathway can make reliably.
honest.why: It is the least reproducible step in the pathway, and the page makes it load-bearing. In CAIRO5 an expert panel agreed unanimously on resectability in only 66% of baseline and 42% of follow-up assessments, and only 12–18% of those patients were judged permanently unresectable. In CLOCC unresectability was decided by each local multidisciplinary team with no central review. In TransMet an independent panel rejected 40% of the patients local boards had declared eligible. In the HAI conversion series resectability was adjudicated by the same surgeons who then operated, and the authors note that the criteria differ between trials so resection rates cannot be compared. The written record the roadmap requires is the right response to this, but it documents a judgement, not a measurement.

honest.t: Conversion and complete-local-treatment rates can be compared between studies.
honest.why: They cannot. Each study defines its own unresectability and scores its own endpoint: 51% versus 37% complete local treatment in CAIRO5 by panel judgement, 54% versus 53% R0/R1 with ablation or SBRT in TRICE judged locally, 47% conversion in a single-centre HAI series adjudicated by the operating surgeons, 17% versus 16% hepatic resection in the pooled radioembolisation analysis. None of these is the same observation, and a programme that benchmarks itself against one of them is measuring its own selection as much as its results.

honest.t: A deeper radiological response produces more clearance.
honest.why: In the only randomised comparisons that measured both, it did not. In CAIRO5's left-sided RAS and BRAF wild-type comparison, panitumumab raised objective response from 53% to 80% and median depth of response from 33% to 49%, yet complete local treatment was 58% in both arms (p=1.00) and both groups were closed early for futility. TRICE deepened response (median 59.6% versus 55.0%, p=0.039) without raising resection (54.2% versus 52.7%). SIRFLOX raised liver response and complete response without changing the resection rate (13.7% versus 14.2%), and the pooled radioembolisation analysis raised objective response from 63% to 72% with identical resection rates (17% versus 16%). FIRE-3's shrinkage advantage was never tested against a resection endpoint. Shrinkage is less often the limiting factor than the pathway's conversion language implies; anatomy, remnant and surgical willingness usually are.

honest.t: Perioperative chemotherapy for resectable disease is supported by EORTC 40983.
honest.why: That trial missed its primary endpoint as randomised (3-year progression-free survival HR 0.79, p=0.058), reached significance only in eligible and resected subsets, showed no overall survival difference at 8.5 years (HR 0.88, p=0.34), did not raise the resection rate (83% versus 84%), and raised reversible postoperative complications from 16% to 25%. Only 63% of patients started the postoperative half, so the regimen actually tested was six preoperative cycles of FOLFOX4. It enrolled one to four metastases with 52% solitary — the most favourable population — while this page directs the regimen at more or larger metastases and a risk score above 2, where it was never tested. ASCO's six-month duration is taken from the same trial, and the one other randomised adjuvant trial ASCO cites, JCOG0603, improved disease-free survival without improving overall survival.

honest.t: Anti-EGFR therapy is the clear first-line choice for left-sided RAS wild-type disease.
honest.why: The guideline recommendation is strong, but the trial evidence behind it is inconsistent and was not designed to answer the question. FIRE-3's prespecified primary endpoint, investigator-assessed response, was negative and progression-free survival was identical; the 72% versus 56% response figure comes from a blinded central review performed after the survival difference was known, and FIRE-3 reported no sidedness analysis and no secondary resection data. CALGB/SWOG 80405 found no survival difference (30.0 versus 29.0 months, HR 0.88, p=0.08), collected sidedness post hoc by chart review, and did not randomise the chemotherapy backbone, so the mFOLFOX6 subgroup favouring cetuximab is an unplanned subgroup of a non-randomised comparison. ASCO's HR 0.71 on the left and 1.35 on the right is a synthesis of retrospectively defined subgroups. The linked editorial's point stands: absence of a difference does not make the two antibodies interchangeable, and a difference in subgroups does not make the choice settled.

honest.t: Second-line radioembolisation benefits patients with liver-dominant disease.
honest.why: EPOCH met both co-primary surrogate endpoints and neither reflects survival: progression-free survival gained 0.8 months, hepatic progression-free survival about 1.9 months, and overall survival was 14.0 versus 14.4 months (HR 1.07, 0.86–1.32) in a trial not powered for it. Grade 3 or worse events were 68.4% versus 49.3%, with three possibly related deaths from radiation-induced liver disease, hepatic failure and portal hypertension at 3 to 5 months — hepatic reserve spent on a surrogate. Thirteen per cent of those assigned never received the treatment, the control arm gave a first-line EGFR inhibitor to only 17% of patients, and the device manufacturer sponsored the trial and co-authored the report. ASCO does not recommend SIRT routinely at all, judging harms to outweigh benefits. The roadmap keeps it as a control option, which is defensible; describing it as treatment that lengthens life is not.

honest.t: Sidedness or RAS status identifies the patients who benefit from radioembolisation.
honest.why: The two datasets point in opposite directions. EPOCH's progression-free survival benefit sat in KRAS-mutant (HR 0.57) and left-sided (HR 0.65) disease with none for right-sided primaries; the pooled FOXFIRE, SIRFLOX and FOXFIRE-Global analysis found its only favourable subgroup in right-sided primaries (overall survival HR 0.67), the mirror image. Both are post hoc, in different microsphere types, different lines and different chemotherapy backbones, and the pooled analysis also reduced oxaliplatin dose around the radioembolisation by protocol. Neither signal should be used to select a patient.

honest.t: DEBIRI prolongs survival in refractory liver-dominant disease.
honest.why: The 22-versus-15-month figure comes from a single two-centre trial of 74 patients against FOLFIRI containing no oxaliplatin, bevacizumab or anti-EGFR agent and capped at eight cycles, while DEBIRI patients could be retreated; the arms therefore differ in treatment intensity (70 procedures against 277 cycles) as well as route. Response was scored by RECIST or EASL at investigator discretion in an open-label trial, DEBIRI patients received prophylactic morphine, steroids and antibiotics before symptom scoring, the report contradicts itself on two p values, and the authors present the work as sizing an effect for a larger trial that has not reproduced this magnitude.

honest.t: Adjuvant hepatic arterial infusion after resection is established.
honest.why: The randomised evidence is one 1999 single-centre trial in which the whole overall survival curves did not differ (p=0.21); the positive result is a prespecified two-year landmark against bolus fluorouracil, and biliary toxicity meant only 26% of patients received more than half the planned floxuridine, so the regimen tested is not the regimen designed. The 2368-patient propensity series spans 21 years, its hepatic arterial infusion patients were six years younger and more recently treated, a published letter argued the propensity model and post-adjustment balance were reported in too little detail to assess, and the largest effects fell in node-negative and low-risk patients — the opposite of where a regional therapy should help most, and with no benefit at all with extrahepatic disease or a positive margin. The confirmatory PUMP trial is in this depot only as a protocol; it gives pump floxuridine without concurrent systemic chemotherapy in clinical risk score 0–2 patients, so neither result will test what this page describes.

honest.t: SBRT is a definitive local treatment for colorectal liver metastases.
honest.why: Its local-control evidence is better than its cure evidence, and almost none of it is colorectal. The 95% and 92% in-field control figures come from a 47-patient single-arm phase I/II trial in which 15 patients had colorectal metastases, colorectal outcomes were never reported separately, 13 patients were treated below 60 Gy, control was scored in only 49 of 63 lesions, and the authors say the competing risk of death may exaggerate it. SABR-COMET is a 99-patient phase 2 screening trial run at a two-sided alpha of 0.20 whose primary report gave p=0.090 for survival; 18 of 99 patients had a colorectal primary and one of the 12 five-year survivors, the survival effect falls to p=0.085 when prostate cancers are removed, liver lesional control was 50% — the lowest of any treated site — and treatment-related mortality was 4.5%. ASCO graded its own SBRT recommendation low quality, weak. Imaging response after SBRT is not a margin.

honest.t: A confirmed ablative margin is the same clearance as a pathologic margin.
honest.why: It is a different observation. A resection margin is read by a pathologist; an ablation margin is inferred by subtracting landmark distances on pre- and post-ablation CT, was unmeasurable in 25% of tumours in the series the 5 mm threshold comes from, and has never been confirmed histologically. That series also improved its margins and its local recurrence rate at the same time as it introduced immediate triple-phase CT, over a decade in which operators, imaging and systemic therapy all changed, so the before-and-after comparison overstates what margin assessment alone delivers. In COLLISION an imaging margin under 5 mm was recorded in only 5% of ablated tumours but 47% of those progressed, while a pathologic R1 was found in 12% of resected tumours and 36% of those progressed — the two measures do not agree on how often clearance failed.

honest.t: The survival figures on this page describe what the first operation achieves.
honest.why: They describe first treatment plus salvage, and the salvage is not incidental. In the ablation series median overall survival was 65 months with no liver progression, 51 months when progression was re-ablated and 22 months once a patient was no longer an ablation candidate. After transplantation 74% recurred in TransMet and 48% in SECA-II, with 5-year progression-free survival of 19.9%; most recurrences were pulmonary and the long survival depends on resecting them under immunosuppression — 46% of isolated recurrences in TransMet were treated with curative intent. Both transplant cohorts' authors state that relapse-free survival is not a valid efficacy measure in this setting, which is another way of saying the result belongs to the whole programme rather than to the operation.

honest.t: TransMet shows 73% five-year survival after transplantation.
honest.why: That is the per-protocol figure, and the protocol deviations ran in both directions: 9 of 47 patients allocated to transplantation never received a graft and 9 of 47 allocated to chemotherapy went on to hepatectomy or transplantation, so the per-protocol comparison is no longer randomised. The intention-to-treat estimate is 56.6% versus 12.6% (HR 0.37, 0.21–0.65), and even that mixes treatments. Proportional hazards did not hold, so the authors added a post-hoc restricted-mean analysis giving a 12.6-month survival gain at 60 months (4.9–20.4). Severe morbidity was 34%, retransplantation 8%, three-month mortality 3%.

honest.t: A transplant programme can reproduce the published survival with the same criteria.
honest.why: The published survival is a product of selection and of an allocation arrangement as much as of the criteria. TransMet depended on negotiated national prioritisation that delivered grafts at a median 50.5 days after randomisation and within two months of the last chemotherapy cycle; 19% of the transplantation arm still never received a graft, and without exception points these normal-liver, low-MELD patients do not compete, so a longer wait raises that dropout. The Oslo programme's own simulation found 2 to 3 eligible patients per year in a population of 5.5 million, and its 15 SECA-II transplants over five years were possible because of a national graft surplus. The North American living-donor series transplanted 10 of 91 evaluated patients and does not report what happened to the other 79.

honest.t: Living-donor transplantation is an established route for this indication.
honest.why: The published North American experience is 10 recipients across three centres running three different protocols, with 1.5-year overall survival 100% and recurrence-free survival 62%; three recurrences occurred at 92, 121 and 199 days, nine explants contained viable tumour and one a positive portal node. The invited commentary calls this a technical demonstration of an already-established operation rather than an oncologic result, notes the 30% early recurrence rate would alarm in any other transplant-oncology indication, and questions using a healthy donor while the deceased-donor pool and machine perfusion are expanding. IHPBA permits living donation only at benchmark-meeting centres and preferably within a trial, and allows no retransplantation for recurrent metastases.

honest.t: MSI-high and mismatch-repair-deficient patients are excluded from transplantation on evidence.
honest.why: They are excluded on a mechanism. The IHPBA statement rests on the risk of graft rejection if immunotherapy were needed after transplant, not on transplant outcome data in these patients, and its own reviewers call it the statement most likely to be overtaken; ESMO 2026 sets no MSI exclusion. The checkpoint evidence does not resolve the dilemma it creates. In CheckMate 8HW overall survival is still masked and the treatment lines are masked, so whether adding ipilimumab helps in the first line is unknown and high-grade toxicity roughly doubled. In KEYNOTE-177, 29.4% of pembrolizumab patients had progressive disease as best response with no biomarker to identify them, survival was blinded with 59% effective crossover, and only about 9% of patients in either arm had curative-intent surgery and were censored at it. Nothing published tells a surgeon what to do with liver-limited dMMR disease that could be cleared.

honest.t: The sequence of primary and liver surgery can be set from the evidence.
honest.why: It cannot. The sequencing recommendations are Delphi expert opinion, and the panel records that no strong evidence supports its central position of chemotherapy before colon resection; the registry comparisons behind it are non-randomised and selection-confounded, with 5-year survival no better for chemotherapy first than for primary surgery first (42% versus 47% in resectable and 31% versus 33% in unresectable disease). The Chinese 2024 consensus prefers simultaneous resection for synchronous disease at its own weakest grade, the opposite emphasis. No randomised trial compares any of these sequences, so the roadmap's rule — sequence by the dominant oncologic threat — is a reasonable principle standing in for absent evidence.

honest.t: The Fong clinical risk score stratifies this population.
honest.why: It stratifies the population it was built from. It was derived and tested in the same 1001 consecutive resections at one tertiary centre with no independent validation cohort, in the pre-oxaliplatin, pre-PET, pre-RAS era, and 123 patients had no preoperative CEA. The two strongest predictors it identified — a positive margin and extrahepatic disease — were deliberately left out because they are not known before the operation, so the score omits the factors that most determined outcome. Its discussants argued that CEA and nodal status double-count tumour burden and that lesion number should not restrict exploration in the ablation era, and warned the score would be misread as an argument against operating. The molecular classifier that improves on it raises the concordance statistic only from 0.55 to 0.62, needs mRNA and miRNA from the resected metastasis, and so cannot inform the preoperative decision the score was built for.

honest.t: The imaging, interval and threshold requirements on this page rest on evidence of benefit.
honest.why: Most of them rest on documents. There is no comparative outcome evidence in CRLM that MRI-based or PET-based staging, a particular reassessment interval, a particular remnant threshold or a particular surveillance schedule changes survival; they are guideline, consensus and local-policy positions, and the page grades them accordingly. The Chinese 2024 consensus publishes four pages of numbered recommendations with its evidence base in an online supplement and describes no consensus method, so its grades cannot be audited from the paper and its CSCO grades are not comparable with ESMO, NCCN or ASCO grades read alongside them. The OPTN transplant-oncology document is review-board guidance and not Policy, and two of its numeric boundaries are internally inconsistent: the initial exclusion is CEA above 80 µg/L while renewal wording is below 80, and progression is defined as a 10% increase in diameter while being labelled RECIST 1.1.

honest.t: Histotripsy is a liver-directed treatment option.
honest.why: In CRLM it is a device with no oncologic outcome data. The pivotal experience is single-arm, 47 patients and 52 tumours, median treated diameter 1.3 cm, 88% of targets in segments II to IV and none in VII or VIII — so the anatomy where an alternative to resection is most wanted was not tested. The headline 90% local control is a post hoc read made once all one-year imaging was available; the prespecified primary assessment gave 63.4%, and the two reads agreed only 71–84% of the time. Twelve-month overall survival among the metastatic patients was 48.6%, treatments after day 30 were not tracked so no progression-free survival exists, and the manufacturer funded the trial and supplied the devices. FDA clearance for tumour destruction is not evidence of benefit.

board: Submission: an Epic form captures the clinical question, phase, disease extent, biology, prior treatment, transplant status, referring clinician and urgency. Owner: submitting clinician.
Triage: the coordinator and a clinically trained gatekeeper check completeness, imaging quality, duplicate cases, the urgent lane and pathology needs. Owner: coordinator with an APP or physician.
Agenda: stable at least 24 hours ahead, target 10–12 decision cases, incomplete routine cases deferred, urgent exceptions by chair approval. Owner: coordinator and chair.

Attendance: hepatobiliary and transplant surgery, medical oncology, diagnostic radiology, interventional radiology, radiation oncology and colorectal surgery are required; pathology when pre-identified; nursing, navigation and the coordinator attend. Owner: programme leadership.
Pathology pre-alert: cases needing tissue or molecular review are flagged at triage so results are available at discussion. Owner: coordinator and pathology.
Urgent lane: a same or next business day pathway for obstructing, bleeding or rapidly progressing patients, with chair approval and a named owner at intake. Owner: chair and coordinator.

Conference: state the question, radiology first, then clinical context, phase assignment, an explicit clearance assessment, options compared with evidence labels, and the chair synthesises one recommendation. Name uncertainty rather than forcing consensus. Owner: a neutral clinical chair.

Documentation: an Epic note within one business day recording the phase, the recommendation, the alternatives considered, the owner, the due date and the reassessment plan. Owner: the designated documenting clinician.
Closure: the registry tracks completion, outside communication, scheduling barriers, results and re-presentation. Owner: navigator and coordinator.

Community relationship: return the recommendation promptly and state whether treatment remains local or transfers; do not absorb longitudinal care without the referring clinician's agreement. Owner: treating and referring clinicians.

These operating requirements are reproduced from the Memorial Hermann HCC roadmap so that one tumour board runs one standard across hepatobiliary diseases. They are evidence grade D by construction and should be audited for adherence, not effectiveness.
dashboard: Clearance discipline: proportion of non-clearance treatment decisions that record why resection, margin-verified ablation, augmentation, staged surgery and HAI were each unsuitable — the pathway's central claim. Target 95% or more.
Staging adequacy: liver MRI obtained before any hepatectomy or ablation, and PET/CT and colonoscopy before transplant evaluation. Target 90% or more.
Molecular completeness: RAS, BRAF, MMR/MSI and HER2 resulted before the first-line systemic therapy decision. Target 90% or more.
Reassessment cadence: surgical reassessment of resectability at least every 8 weeks during conversion-intent therapy. Target 85% or more.
Ablation quality: confirmed circumferential margin documented, proportion with a margin under 5 mm, and local progression at 12 and 24 months. Margin documented in 95% or more; track progression.
Perioperative safety: 90-day morbidity and mortality by procedure type, including augmentation and staged strategies. Risk-adjusted quarterly review.

Transplant pathway: time from declaration of permanent unresectability to transplant evaluation, protocol conformance, registry entry, waitlist dropout, and recurrence site and management. 100% registry entry, quarterly review.
Systemic care: line, regimen, molecular match, response, grade 3 or worse toxicity and trial enrolment. Quarterly review.
Equity: delays and treatment completion by payer, language, geography, race and ethnicity, and referring site. Identify and act; no punitive target.

approvals.q: Name the accountable CRLM pathway owner and the neutral tumour-board chair.
approvals.why: The pathway produces one recommendation, one accountable owner, one due date and one reassessment plan; without a named owner and a neutral chair the synthesis step has nobody to perform it.
approvals.audit: Named individuals recorded in the programme charter, with the chair's name on every conference record.

approvals.q: Approve the Epic submission form with an explicit phase field and a clearance-assessment field.
approvals.why: Phase assignment and the explicit clearance question are the two things this pathway is built on, so they have to be captured at submission rather than reconstructed later.
approvals.audit: Completeness of the phase and clearance fields at triage; the clearance-discipline dashboard measure depends on them.

approvals.q: Decide whether Memorial Hermann will run a hepatic arterial infusion programme, and if so the credentialing standard, case volume floor and toxicity review cadence.
approvals.why: HAI conversion evidence is single-arm and concentrated in experienced centres, and biliary toxicity and pump complications are not occasional-case risks; the modality is only defensible with a credentialed programme behind it.
approvals.audit: Credentialing records, case volume against the floor, and the 6-month grade 3 or worse toxicity and biliary toxicity review.

approvals.q: Ratify the written liver transplant protocol for CRLM: eligibility, review-board route, graft strategy including living donation, registry dataset and recurrence plan.
approvals.why: CRLM is not a standardised OPTN exception, so the institutional protocol is the operative constraint and the programme domain of the selection table requires it in writing.
approvals.audit: Protocol conformance and registry entry for every listed patient, reviewed quarterly.

approvals.q: Set the institutional position on transplanting outside TransMet criteria — permitted under protocol with registry entry, or not at all.
approvals.why: There is no randomised evidence outside the TransMet population, and the roadmap lists this among the statements that are locally reasonable but not evidence based.
approvals.audit: Mandatory registry recording whether criteria were met or exceeded, recurrence site and post-recurrence survival.

approvals.q: Define the pre-transplant checkpoint-inhibitor policy for MSI-high candidates, including washout and the approval route, before any such patient is listed.
approvals.why: The exception route requires microsatellite stability and IHPBA excludes these patients, while pre-transplant checkpoint exposure and post-transplant rejection risk must be addressed before the first dose.
approvals.audit: Written policy in place before listing; every exposed candidate has a documented graft-safety assessment.

approvals.q: Approve remnant-volume thresholds and the augmentation strategy hierarchy (PVE, LVD, two-stage, ALPPS), including who decides between them.
approvals.why: Modality-specific remnant thresholds are local policy without comparative outcome evidence, and the augmentation options differ in morbidity rather than in proven survival.
approvals.audit: Perioperative safety measure by procedure type, including augmentation and staged strategies, plus resection rate and dropout between stages.

approvals.q: Set the minimum ablative margin that counts toward clearance, and require it to be documented.
approvals.why: Ablation counts as clearance only when a circumferential margin is confirmed, and local progression risk rises steeply below 5 mm.
approvals.audit: Margin documented in 95% or more of ablations, with local progression reported by achieved margin band at 12 and 24 months.

approvals.q: Name the referral route and the specialist team for peritoneal metastases, which are assessed outside this liver pathway.
approvals.why: Peritoneal disease is assessed by a peritoneal surface malignancy team rather than routed automatically through the liver pathway, and any peritoneal disease ends transplant intent.
approvals.audit: Referral route documented; cases with peritoneal disease tracked out of the liver pathway rather than treated as an extension of it.

approvals.q: Decide which transplant criteria set governs locally, and record the resolution of each named disagreement between the OPTN guidance route, IHPBA 2021 and ESMO 2026 — MSI-high and dMMR status, BRAF V600E versus any BRAF mutation, the metabolic tumour volume and total lesion glycolysis bars, the months of stability required and the line of therapy by which transplantation may be considered.
approvals.why: The documents a review board will be handed disagree on gates that decide individual patients, and the rule that the stricter governs does not by itself say which document supplies the stricter value for each criterion.
approvals.audit: A single written criteria table in the protocol, with the source of every gate named and every conflict shown as resolved; conformance checked for each listed patient.

approvals.q: Resolve the two numeric boundaries in the OPTN transplant-oncology guidance before the first filing: a CEA of exactly 80 µg/L, and the definition of progression as a 10% increase in diameter while being labelled RECIST 1.1.
approvals.why: The initial exclusion is stated as CEA above 80 and the renewal wording as below 80, so an exact value of 80 has no stated answer; and the 10% figure differs from the usual target-lesion threshold, so a candidate can be progressing under one reading and stable under the other.
approvals.audit: Both boundaries addressed in writing, with the source wording preserved rather than silently substituted, before any exception request is submitted.

approvals.q: Decide whether anti-EGFR therapy is used with conversion intent in left-sided RAS and BRAF wild-type disease, or only as the first-line survival choice.
approvals.why: In the one randomised comparison that measured clearance, panitumumab raised objective response from 53% to 80% and deepened response without changing complete local treatment (58% in both arms), and those groups were closed early for futility; the conversion rationale and the first-line rationale are not the same claim.
approvals.audit: Conversion-intent regimen recorded against the stated indication, with the complete-local-treatment rate reported by regimen.

approvals.q: Set the institutional position on transarterial therapy in refractory disease: whether second-line Y90 and DEBIRI are offered at all, and the requirement that every transarterial treatment be recorded as regional control with a named reassessment date.
approvals.why: Neither improved overall survival — EPOCH gave 14.0 versus 14.4 months with grade 3 or worse events in 68% and three treatment-related deaths, and the DEBIRI survival figure comes from 74 patients against an obsolete comparator — and ASCO does not recommend SIRT routinely at all.
approvals.audit: Every transarterial case recorded with intent, reassessment date and hepatic reserve before and after; cumulative radiation record maintained and HAI eligibility checked before liver irradiation.

approvals.q: Decide whether perioperative chemotherapy is offered outside the population in which it was tested — one to four metastases, no extrahepatic disease — and require the indication to be recorded each time it is given.
approvals.why: EORTC 40983 missed its primary endpoint, showed no survival difference at 8.5 years, did not raise the resection rate and raised postoperative complications; extending it to higher-burden disease and a risk score above 2 is a local judgement that should be visible as one.
approvals.audit: Indication recorded for every perioperative course, with 90-day complications and resection rate reported against the recorded indication.

approvals.q: Decide how an ablation margin that cannot be measured is recorded and managed, and who reads the confirmatory study.
approvals.why: In the series the 5 mm threshold comes from, the margin was unmeasurable in a quarter of tumours and never confirmed histologically, and in COLLISION the imaging and pathologic margin categories did not agree on how often clearance failed; an unreadable margin is a decision, not a gap in the record.
approvals.audit: Proportion of ablations with an unmeasurable margin, what was done next, and local progression in that group at 12 and 24 months.

approvals.q: Commit the surveillance and salvage capacity the published survival figures depend on — thoracic surveillance, pulmonary metastasectomy, repeat hepatic clearance — and name the owner of each.
approvals.why: After transplantation three-quarters of TransMet patients and half of SECA-II patients recurred, mostly in the lung, and the survival gain came from treating those recurrences with curative intent; the ablation series shows the same pattern, with median survival falling from 51 to 22 months once a patient is no longer a candidate for re-treatment.
approvals.audit: Recurrence site, time to detection, treatment given and post-recurrence survival for every cleared and transplanted patient, reviewed quarterly.

approvals.q: Agree the registry dataset for every conversion-intent course: who judged resectability at each reassessment, what they judged, and whether the operation happened.
approvals.why: Resectability judgements are the least reproducible step in this pathway — unanimous in only 66% of baseline and 42% of follow-up panel assessments in CAIRO5, and locally determined with no central review in the other conversion series — so conversion rates are uninterpretable without recording who decided.
approvals.audit: Named assessor and judgement at each reassessment; conversion rate and time from first response to operation reported from that record.

approvals.q: Pilot for 90 days, audit 20 consecutive cases, then revise before approval as a clinical practice guideline.
approvals.why: This is a draft for multidisciplinary and institutional governance review, not active clinical policy, and the operating measures are grade D by construction.
approvals.audit: The 20-case audit against the dashboard measures, with revisions recorded before approval.

provenance: Built from the Memorial Hermann Colorectal Liver Metastasis System Roadmap Draft v0.6 (4 October 2026, liver-directed section revised 3 October 2026, evidence current to 20 September 2026) and its companion guideline alignment worksheet of the same date, which supplied the institutional positions, the NCCN decisions 1-16 and the open ratification items. Revised on 7 October 2026 (Batch 08) after a full-text read of the whole CRLM reference depot: 45 papers, each with an independently recorded critique, covering all 45 PubMed-indexed references cited on this page. Every evidence string was re-checked against the paper's own reported results rather than against a guideline quoting it, and the grades were re-set where the full text showed the recommendation rested on a surrogate endpoint, a subset analysis, an unvalidated threshold or a single centre's practice; 20 evidence entries changed and 13 grades were lowered in that pass, and the honest section was rewritten and expanded from 5 entries to 27. Three references are cited only for what they do not yet show: the PUMP trial appears as a published protocol with no outcome data, so no efficacy claim rests on it; the LIGRO survival analysis is published separately and was not read, so ALPPS is cited for resectability only; and the NCCN guideline, the OPTN policy and guidance documents, the Memorial Hermann roadmap and its alignment worksheet are not PubMed-indexed papers and were read as documents, not trials. Policy wording follows NCCN Colon Cancer v2.2026 (7 April 2026), OPTN Policy 9 as retrieved 1 October 2026, and the OPTN Adult MELD Exceptions for Transplant Oncology review-board guidance of December 2025, which is guidance and not Policy. The roadmap itself is a draft pending multidisciplinary and institutional governance review: it is not active clinical policy, does not replace clinician judgement, current drug labelling, OPTN policy or patient-specific informed consent, and every transplant criterion must be confirmed against current policy at implementation.
